name: お好み焼き 鉄板焼き こひなた (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Kohinata)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is made on a shared teppan griddle using wheat batter and wheat noodles, so cross-contact with gluten is inherent across the menu.
Dishes are finished with sweet okonomiyaki sauce (Otafuku-style), which is made with wheat.
Everything is cooked on one shared griddle alongside pork, egg, and seafood, so vegan separation is not feasible.

name: お好み焼き・鉄板焼き 蔵屋 紙屋町店 (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Kuraya Kamiyacho-ten)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki, noodles, and griddle dishes share a common teppan; wheat batter and wheat-based sauces are central to the menu, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Standard Japanese soy sauce and okonomiyaki sauce (both typically wheat-containing) are used; no gluten-free sauce is mentioned.
All seats use a shared iron griddle that cooks oysters, beef, pork, and seafood, so any vegetable item would contact animal products.

name: 尾道ラーメン 暁 (Onomichi Ramen Akatsuki)

claims.text: The kitchen works with wheat noodles and a wheat-based soy sauce broth throughout, so any non-wheat order would face heavy cross-contamination; no allergen separation is documented.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) base with a scorched-soy-sauce aroma; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Broth is made from pork and chicken stock with rendered pork back-fat, so all dishes share animal-based stock.

name: 御食事処 山一本店 (Oshokuji Dokoro Yamaichi Honten)

claims.text: The signature anago-meshi is finished with a soy-sauce-based tare, which in Japan virtually always contains wheat; tempura and oyster dishes likewise involve wheat.
The kitchen is centered on fish and shellfish (conger eel, oysters) and fish-based dashi, so cross-contact with animal products is pervasive throughout the menu.

name: お食事処 大和屋 (Oshokuji-dokoro Yamatoya)

claims.text: The signature anago-meshi and other dishes are finished with a soy-based sauce, which in Japan is normally brewed with wheat and is not gluten-free.

name: お食事処 大たに (Oshokujidokoro Otani)

claims.text: Anago and rice-bowl dishes are served with Japanese soy sauce and tare, which are standard wheat-containing seasonings; no gluten-free alternative is mentioned.
The menu centers on oysters, conger eel and other seafood plus meat and egg donburi, with fish-based dashi broths; there are no documented vegan items or separate vegan preparation.

name: お食事処 梅山 (Oshokujidokoro Umeyama)

claims.text: The signature anago-don is finished with a house sweet-savory sauce that is soy-sauce based, which in Japan standardly contains wheat; oyster udon uses wheat noodles and fried oysters use wheat batter.
The menu is entirely seafood-based (conger eel, oysters, shellfish) with dashi and soy seasonings; no plant-only preparations are documented.

name: お食事処 よさこい (Oshokujidokoro Yosakoi)

claims.text: Anago and oyster dishes and okonomiyaki are standard Hiroshima preparations that use wheat-based soy sauce/tare and wheat-flour batter; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
An English menu is available, which can help travelers identify ingredients before ordering.
